fixes.explanation: A great feast, baker! Genesis 21:8 says Abraham held it on the day Isaac was weaned. The child grew, and then came the day for the table. I've been to a few cookie-box parties where the guest of honor was a toddler, and I promise you the toddler ate the least and wore the most.

No shoving in this verse, friend. The text says Sarah saw the boy "mocking her son" (Genesis 21:9). He's Ishmael, Hagar's son. Mocking is the only thing the verse puts in his hands, so I won't add a push to it.

Ignoring would be quieter than what Sarah saw, friend. Genesis 21:9 says the boy was "mocking her son." That's Ishmael, the son of Hagar the Egyptian. Ignoring is doing nothing at all, and the verse has him doing something.

Beersheba, baker! Genesis 21:14 says Hagar left and wandered in the Wilderness of Beersheba, with bread and a skin of water on her shoulders and her boy beside her. A wilderness with no clear road is the kind of place where even a good map gives up. Hold onto that name, because the next part of her story happens out there.

Yes, baker. She says, "I cannot bear to watch the boy die!" (Genesis 21:16). The text says she sat down about a bowshot away, and that she lifted up her voice and wept. I think that's a mother in deep anguish. This is one of the heavy parts of the story.
